claims.text: Selecting specific alloying elements in refractory HEAs will produce a low-activation material.
The resulting refractory HEA will be suitable as a structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The initial refractory HEAs contain standard alloying elements.
Specific low-activation alloying elements can be selected to modify the HEA composition.
The intended service conditions are high-temperature conditions typical of fusion reactors.
The choice of alloying elements determines the relevant compositional mediator.
Selecting low-activation alloying elements will reduce the overall activation of the HEA.
Selecting low-activation alloying elements will maintain or enhance the mechanical properties required for high-temperature applications.
The modified HEA will have lower activation levels than standard refractory HEAs.
The modified HEA will retain mechanical properties suitable for high-temperature plasma-facing components.
Standard refractory HEAs have higher activation levels than the proposed modified HEAs.
The hypothesis applies only to high-temperature fusion-reactor applications.
The effects of specific alloying-element selections on activation and mechanical properties cannot be established without empirical data.
